title: Close matmul GF(2) small-n (n=64, n=256) to M4RI parity
description:
Close the last two bare-FAIL cells in the 026fc832 SOTA scorecard: matmul GF(2) (BitMatrix × BitMatrix) at n=64 and n=256, which sit above the 1.5× M4RI threshold (A8 rows 4-5).

## Background

Annex A8 of the predecessor scorecard (`97bf0879`) routed matmul GF(2) n=64,256 to story `974a85bd` ("Close GF(2) BitMatrix gaps to M4RI"). But `974a85bd`'s parity report (`dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-111a3967-gf2-parity-evidence.md`) only dispositioned the matmul **target rows** n=1024 (1.18× PASS) and n=4096 (1.50× PASS); it did NOT cover n=64,256, which sit below the M4RM (Method-of-4-Russians) crossover where M4RI's optimized small-n path wins. The 026fc832 final scorecard (`b0fa00af`) surfaced these as the sole unresolved bare-FAIL cells. Per user decision 2026-05-28, this successor task is filed to **close them** (not amend/exclude).

Current production matmul dispatch (per `974a85bd` § 2.1) uses a "Narrow" tier (stride_words < 16, 64 KiB table budget, k ≤ 8) for n < 1024. The small-n schedule has not been tuned against M4RI at n=64,256.

## Scope

Engineer the small-n GF(2) M4RM matmul path (n=64, n=256) to within 1.5× of M4RI on the pinned reference, following the PPC optimization spiral (measure -> inspect asm -> tune k-block / table budget / memory layout / consider a direct word-level kernel for n<=64). Update production dispatch (the narrow-tier schedule selection in `gf2-core/src/alg/` M4RM, plus any `gf2-kernels-simd` kernel) as needed. Unsafe stays in `gf2-kernels-simd`; `gf2-core` stays `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] matmul GF(2) at n=64 and n=256 (uniform regime): Ratio = gf2 wall / M4RI wall <= 1.5x on a 5-trial CCX1-pinned bench on the 5900X reference host. M4RI baseline (pinned `dev/bench_results/2026-04-26-reference.csv`): n=64 uniform = 3474 ns, n=256 uniform = 29808 ns. Targets: gf2 n=64 <= 5211 ns, gf2 n=256 <= 44712 ns.
- [hard] No regression on the matmul GF(2) cells already PASSing at n=1024 (1.18x) and n=4096 (1.50x) -- delta <= 5% vs the `8e305c21` / `974a85bd` production baseline.
- [hard] Bit-exact correctness preserved: proptests for matmul GF(2) at boundary lengths {0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65} plus n=64,256 against a scalar/naive reference.
- [hard] No unsafe leaks outside `gf2-kernels-simd`; `gf2-core` stays `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.
- [hard] Evidence doc records pre/post numbers, the M4RI baseline + source, non-regression sweep, and reproducibility commands; attached via `jit doc add`.
- If closure to <= 1.5x proves structurally infeasible after a genuine PPC-spiral engineering attempt, document the cause with measured evidence (asm, schedule sweep) and escalate to the lead -- do NOT silently amend or exclude. The [aspirational]/EXCLUDED path is available only with explicit user approval backed by infeasibility evidence.

## Out of scope

- matmul GF(2) n >= 1024 (already PASS via `974a85bd`).
- AVX-512 (epic `7f809931`).
- BLAS / external dependencies.
- Other GF(2) operations (echelon, invert, solve, pluq) -- dispositioned elsewhere.

## Notes

- Filed 2026-05-28 per user escalation decision (option B: file successor) on epic 026fc832's `b0fa00af` blocker.
- Disposition target for `b0fa00af` A8 rows 4-5. `b0fa00af` depends on this issue; the scorecard's rows 4-5 update to PASS (or, only with user approval + evidence, AMENDED) once this lands.
- Reference host: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X (Zen 3), AVX2+FMA, no AVX-512.
- M4RM kernel lives in `crates/gf2-core/src/alg/`; production schedule selection per `974a85bd` § 2.1 (narrow/mid/wide/wider tiers).
